# Layers and the include order

Which way dependencies may point inside `prosper/src`, and what each layer owns. The order is the
`LAYER_ORDER` constant in `tools/ci/check_arch_ratchet.py`; the table below is generated from it,
so the constant is the single source and this page cannot drift from it. Why each layer sits where
it does, with the include counts behind it, is in `docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE_TARGET_TREE.md`.

<!-- gen:layer-order:begin (generated by tools/docs/check_arch_docs.py --write) -->
| rank | layer | may include |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 0 | `self` | itself only |
| 1 | `loader` | itself and `self` |
| 2 | `input` | itself and `self`, `loader` |
| 3 | `diagnostics` | itself and `self`, `loader`, `input` |
| 4 | `host` | itself and `self`, `loader`, `input`, `diagnostics` |
| 5 | `gpu` | itself and `self`, `loader`, `input`, `diagnostics`, `host` |
| 6 | `hle` | itself and `self`, `loader`, `input`, `diagnostics`, `host`, `gpu` |
| -- | `frontends/`, `tests/` | never includable from `prosper/src` |
<!-- gen:layer-order:end -->

## Rules

### LAY-1 -- includes point down the layer order

A file in a layer MAY include its own layer and any layer ranked below it in the table, and MUST
NOT include a layer ranked above it. Existing inversions are baselined and may only shrink; a new
one fails CI.
Status: accepted
Enforcement: ratchet:layer-include

### LAY-2 -- the core never depends on a frontend or a test

Nothing under `prosper/src` includes `frontends/` or `tests/`. The frontends sit on top of the
core and may include all of it; the dependency never runs the other way.
Status: accepted
Enforcement: ratchet:layer-include

### LAY-3 -- shipping code does not live in the test tree

Code that ships in a frontend MUST NOT live under `prosper/tests/` or in the `prosper::test`
namespace. The Vulkan backend in `tests/fixtures/render_runner.h` is the baselined exception, and
its move is ADR 0004.
Status: accepted
Enforcement: ratchet:fixture-include, ratchet:test-dep, adr:0004

### LAY-4 -- the guest layer sits between host and gpu

`src/guest/` holds guest semantics running on the host (ABI bridge, TLS, fault interpretation,
guest memory, image execution, and engines such as APR). It ranks above `host` and below `gpu`, and
`host` shrinks to the OS seam.
Status: proposed (adr:0003)
Enforcement: ratchet:layer-include, adr:0003

### LAY-5 -- the build enforces the order

Each layer is its own CMake library target linked only to the layers below it, so an include
against the order fails to compile rather than failing a text scan. A layer becomes its own target
once its baselined inversions reach zero; until then `LAY-1`'s ratchet holds it.
Status: proposed (adr:0008)
Enforcement: adr:0008

## What each layer owns

| layer | owns | does not own |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `self` | SELF/ELF parsing into host-independent module images | anything about where or how an image runs |
| `loader` | linking modules, the export table, import slots, TLS layout | handler implementations; any OS call |
| `input` | platform-neutral pad state | device backends (those are frontends) |
| `diagnostics` | observe-only instrumentation, the env-switch cache, perf alarms | anything that changes what the guest sees |
| `host` | OS services and, today, guest execution on the host (ADR 0003 splits the two) | Sony library semantics |
| `gpu` | AGC/PM4 decode, GPU state, the RDNA2 recompiler, resources, capture and timeline | Sony library entry points; the Vulkan backend's device ownership |
| `hle` | the reimplemented Sony library surface: NID handlers, argument decoding, return codes | OS calls behind `#if` (see `PLAT-1`); engines that `guest/` should own (ADR 0003) |
